newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat steady as spot demand slows.
newsitem.headline: French wheat steady as spot demand slows.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Thursday amid dwindling demand for spot grain, dealers said.
The market ignored news truckers had voted to keep up a nationwide blockade protest that is now in its 11th day.
Rouen wheat was quoted at 860 francs per tonne for December delivery and at 845 francs for January delivery, both unchanged on Wednesday.
"Buyers are getting less aggressive," a dealer said.
The protests by truckers pushed wheat prices up earlier this week as port silos reported supply disruption and operators scrambled to complete a few cargoes loading in ports.
But dealers said ships had apparently no difficulties loading wheat in Rouen despite disruptions to silos.
Exporters were also awaiting the outcome of the weekly EU grain auction, hoping the EU would raise its export refund.
Traders bidding through France have asked to export 550,700 tonnes of free-market EU soft wheat at rebates ranging from 16.49 to 22.35 Ecus per tonne.
Dealers said the heavy tonnages sought were apparently destined to help cover old export contracts.
One exporter said the EU was likely to raise the export refund on wheat to 18.50 Ecus per tonne from last week's level of 16.59 Ecus.
This would allow the release of some 280,000 tonnes of wheat, he said.
He also calculated a refund of 18.50 Ecus valued EU wheat for late December-early January at around $152 per tonne, Fob.
But that rebate level would still be unsufficient to help EU exporters land fresh export contracts amid fierce competition from other world suppliers, he said.
Wheat futures volume on MATIF was a thin 11 lots, with the May 97 expiry quoted at 874 francs, down three francs from Wednesday.
